Short answer for the sender: No — the sender will not see anything different if you archive vs delete their message. Those actions affect only your copy of the message in your mailbox, not the sender’s copy or any delivery status.

What happens to the message in your account (general terms)
- Archive
  - Removes the message from your Inbox view but keeps it in your mailbox/store.
  - The message is still searchable and retrievable (in an “All Mail,” “Archive,” or similar folder/label).
  - It does not normally count as permanently removed; you can move it back to Inbox or another folder at any time.
- Delete
  - Moves the message to a Trash/Deleted Items folder or marks it for deletion.
  - The message is usually only retained temporarily in Trash/Deleted Items, and will eventually be permanently removed according to your provider’s retention rules (provider-defined).
  - Once permanently deleted (or if you manually empty Trash), it’s generally not recoverable by the end user (admins or backups might still restore it in some systems).

Notes and exceptions to be aware of
- Deleting or archiving affects only your mailbox copy — it does not remove the message from the sender’s mailbox or anyone else who received the message.
- Some clients/protocols behave differently:
  - IMAP: archive typically moves the message to a server-side Archive folder/label; delete usually moves it to Trash or sets a Deleted flag and requires expunge to remove it.
  - POP: behavior depends on client settings — messages can be left on or removed from the server after download.
- Organizational policies, retention rules, or backups on corporate systems can override or extend recoverability after deletion.
